claims.claim: Intersect requests 25,400,000 ADA to fund its core operating model from June 2026 to June 2027.

The budget is allocated as 6,000,000 ADA for operations and ecosystem coordination, 18,800,000 ADA for technical stewardship and incident response, and 600,000 ADA for management of critical processes.
Intersect states the overall ask has decreased from $7.875M last year to $6.35M while preserving the most critical continuity and maturity functions.

Intersect states it has matured over two years into a focused operational layer supporting committees and working groups, core Haskell repository stewardship, upgrades, incident response, and administration of community-approved initiatives.
Intersect states it has coordinated two network upgrades, is preparing for a third, and led ecosystem coordination during the November 2025 chain partition incident.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation and audited results.
The proposal states the requested amount does not breach the 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission and links to the relevant governance action.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverables, controls, spending, and milestone evidence.
Intersect discloses that it and its committees received 22,385,000 ADA in prior Cardano Treasury funding through three governance actions within the past 24 months.

Intersect will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with stated TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based authorization thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The document requests 25,400,000 ADA for Intersect's 2026-2027 governance coordination, technical stewardship, incident response, and critical process management, with budget breakdowns, prior funding disclosure, smart-contract custody details, voting-process references, NCL compliance claims, and planned external assurance.
